title: Ocular Surface Reconstruction: AMG vs. MMG
summary: A comprehensive comparative guide for Ophthalmic surgeons on biological scaffolds. While Amniotic Membrane Grafting (AMG) provides temporary anti-inflammatory and pro-healing support, Mucous Membrane Grafting (MMG) offers permanent structural reconstruction for end-stage ocular surface disease.

sections.title: AMG: The Biological Swiss Army Knife
Indications for AMG (Exhaustive)
content: Persistent Epithelial Defects (PED) unresponsive to medical therapy
Acute Chemical/Thermal Burns (to suppress immediate inflammation)
Acute Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS/TEN) - Grade 1-3
Pterygium surgery (Primary or Recurrent) to reduce recurrence risk
Bullous Keratopathy (Symptomatic pain relief in poor visual potential)
Partial Limbal Stem Cell Deficiency (LSCD)
Filtering Bleb leaks (Glaucoma surgery rescue)
Mooren's Ulcer and peripheral ulcerative keratitis (PUK)
Neurotrophic Keratopathy
Conjunctival Chalasis and symblepharon prevention

sections.title: Indications for MMG (Structural)
content: Chronic Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (Late cicatricial stage)
Ocular Cicatricial Pemphigoid (OCP) - End stage reconstruction
Lid Margin Keratinization (Grafting the posterior lid margin)
Severe Symblepharon or Anophthalmic Socket contraction
Fornix Reconstruction (Restoring depth for motility or prosthetics)
Superior Limbic Keratoconjunctivitis (SLK) - Refractory cases
Severe Trichiasis/Distichiasis causing corneal trauma
Lagophthalmos secondary to cicatricial eyelid shortening

rows: Sutured or glued within the defect edges
Permanent integration, scaffold for epithelial crawl
Combination of Inlay and Overlay layers
Filling deep stromal craters while protecting surface
Sutureless AM held by a polycarbonate ring

sections.title: Harvesting Buccal MMG: Process
content: Step 1: Identify donor site (Buccal mucosa or lower labial mucosa)
Step 2: Local infiltration with Xylocaine 2% + Epinephrine 1:100,000
Step 3: Mark graft size (usually 20% larger to account for shrinkage)
Step 4: Dissect Split-thickness or Full-thickness graft (avoid Stensen's duct!)
Step 5: Defat the graft meticulously using Westcott scissors
Step 6: Secure to ocular surface with 8-0 or 9-0 Vicryl/Silk sutures

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis: When to use which?

rows: Persistent inflammation if basement membrane is lost
Donor site morbidity (pain, scarring, restricted jaw opening)
Keratinization of the graft if ocular surface is extremely dry

sections.title: Critical Red Flags
content: Never use AMG in active infection (Fungal/Bacterial) without antimicrobial coverage.
Avoid harvesting MMG near Stensen's duct (opposite the upper 2nd molar).
MMG will keratinize if the patient has zero tear production (Schirmer 0).
AMG 'epithelium-up' vs 'epithelium-down' matters for integration (Inlay vs Overlay).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Cryopreserved AM (AmnioGraft) retains heavy-chain hyaluronic acid/PTX3 complex, making it superior for anti-inflammation compared to dehydrated AM.
In MMG harvesting, a 'thin' graft is preferred for the lid margin to prevent a bulky look, while a 'thicker' graft is better for deep fornix reconstruction.
Glue (Fibrin/Tisseel) can be used to secure AMG, significantly reducing surgical time and post-op irritation compared to sutures.
The 'Lid Margin Rotation' combined with MMG is the gold standard for treating corneal-chafing keratinized lids in OCP.
For PED, if the AMG melts within 7 days, it suggests a highly proteolytically active ocular surface—consider systemic collagenase inhibitors (Tetracyclines).

sections.title: Landmark Evidence: SJS/TEN
sections.content: The landmark study by Gregory (2011) and later Kim et al. established that AMG applied within the first 72-96 hours of SJS onset significantly reduces long-term visual morbidity from 70% down to less than 10%. MMG remains the secondary choice for rehabilitating those who missed the early AMG window.
